This person helps homeowners navigate the process from their first request for assistance through the completion of their repairs. It requires someone who can listen with compassion, communicate clearly, stay exceptionally organized, and make sure people and projects don’t get lost in the process.

HRM is a growing organization, and we’re looking for someone who can grow with us. The Program Coordinator will help manage the processes, technology, documentation, and workflows that allow our team to serve an increasing number of homeowners.

Serve as a primary point of contact for homeowners throughout the repair process.
Respond to homeowner calls, emails, and applications with warmth, patience, and professionalism.
Screen applicants for eligibility and collect required documentation.

Identify projects that have stalled or need attention and proactively follow up.

Help develop and improve processes as HRM’s project volume, staff, and programs grow.

Benefits

Team environment

What You’ll Do

Homeowner Communication & Coordination

Serve as a primary point of contact for homeowners throughout the repair process.
Respond to homeowner calls, emails, and applications with warmth, patience, and professionalism.
Screen applicants for eligibility and collect required documentation.
Schedule home assessments and repair projects with homeowners, Project Managers, contractors, and trade partners.
Keep homeowners informed about project status, next steps, scheduling, and expectations.
Proactively follow up on outstanding information and help keep projects moving from application through completion.

Project & Program Coordination

Coordinate schedules and workflows across multiple homeowners and repair projects.
Track projects, outstanding tasks, deadlines, and next steps.
Prepare project files and assist with estimates, materials, deliveries, and project documentation.
Identify projects that have stalled or need attention and proactively follow up.
Coordinate volunteer opportunities and maintain required volunteer documentation.
Work closely with Project Managers to ensure they have the information and documentation needed to complete their work.
Help develop and improve processes as HRM’s project volume, staff, and programs grow.

Systems, Data & Reporting

The Program Coordinator helps ensure that HRM’s systems reflect what’s actually happening in the field.
Maintain accurate homeowner, project, and program information in Monday.com, Bloomerang, and Google Workspace.
Use Monday.com to actively manage workflows, project status, deadlines, responsibilities, and follow-up.
Maintain accurate records in Bloomerang and other organizational databases.
Identify missing information or documentation and proactively resolve gaps.
Maintain organized and complete homeowner and project files.
Collect and maintain eligibility information, demographics, project costs, photos, completion documentation, outputs, and other information required for grants and government-funded programs.
Work with leadership and grant/compliance staff to ensure program records are complete, timely, and ready for reporting, reimbursement requests, monitoring, or audits.
Support organizational dashboards and monthly, quarterly, and annual program reporting.
Help evaluate and improve systems and workflows as HRM adds programs, funding sources, staff, and project volume.

Who We’re Looking For

This role requires a unique combination of compassion, organization, initiative, and systems thinking.
The right person:
Genuinely enjoys helping people and communicates with warmth and professionalism.
Takes ownership and follows responsibilities through to completion.
Is exceptionally organized and comfortable managing many moving pieces at once.
Naturally asks, “What’s next, what’s missing, and who needs to know?”
Communicates proactively when something changes, stalls, or needs attention.
Has strong attention to detail and understands that accurate documentation matters.
Is comfortable working extensively in technology and database systems.
Can follow established processes while also recognizing when a process could work better.
Is willing to handle the day-to-day details today while having the ability and desire to take on greater operational responsibility as HRM grows.

Qualifications

3+ years of experience in program coordination, project coordination, construction operations, nonprofit administration, office management, or a related field.
Demonstrated ability to manage workflows, multiple projects, schedules, deadlines, and competing priorities.
Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
Strong technology skills and experience with CRM, project-management, database, or case-management systems.
Strong attention to detail and demonstrated ability to maintain accurate records and documentation.
Experience using Monday.com and/or Bloomerang strongly preferred.
Experience with government-funded programs, grant documentation, compliance, or reporting strongly preferred.
Demonstrated ability to improve processes and create systems that help a team manage increasing volume and complexity.

Benefits

Competitive salary based on experience
Flexible schedule/hybrid
Unlimited PTO
Professional development opportunities
Team environment

How to Apply

This position offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact in the lives of vulnerable homeowners while working within a faith-based dynamic and passionate team. If you are organized, compassionate, and driven to make a difference, we encourage you to apply. Interested candidates should submit their resume and cover letter to info@homerepairs.org.

Working at Yale means contributing to a better tomorrow. Whether you are a current resident of our New Haven-based community, eligible for opportunities through the New Haven Hiring Initiative, or a newcomer, interested in exploring all that Yale has to offer, your talents and contributions are welcome. Discover your opportunities at Yale!

Overview

Reporting to the Planned Giving Program Manager and working with considerable independence and discretion in establishing priorities, the Planned Giving Program Coordinator provides administrative, database and fundraising support to the planned giving team to achieve the unit’s common goals and priorities. In collaboration with frontline fundraisers and other colleagues, the program coordinator supports the identification, solicitation and cultivation of alumni and friends capable of making planned gifts to the university. Essential duties include:

Has responsibility for the tracking, reporting, management, and analysis of activity related to planned giving prospects and all planned gifts using the Hopper/Blackbaud CRM database requiring use of Excel formulas, pivot tables, charts and graphs.
Produces ad hoc reports by assimilating data from primary databases and other sources to support marketing and fundraising efforts.
Supports the Planned Giving staff by drafting a wide variety of written materials; formats, edits/proofreads, and assembles correspondence for the team and others; assists in creating training materials; makes travel arrangements, produces travel itineraries; prepares expense reports; responds to phone calls, e-mail, and mail from alumni, donors and staff, providing initial response and follow-up to inquiries as needed; performs data entry and filing, and sends group mail/email.
Prepares gift proposals and illustrations, tax information, and other documents related to life income gifts and bequests.
Works closely with colleagues in Gift & Records Services, with other areas of the university, and with BNY Mellon Charitable Gift Services in the administration of Yale’s Life Income Program.
Participates in a comprehensive stewardship strategy for Yale’s planned gift and bequest recognition society, Yale Legacy Partners.
Assists with logistics for Yale Legacy Partner events and coordinates regional meetings including donor-hosted gatherings and other special occasions.
Contacts hosts, drafts invitations, creates invitation lists, confirms attendance, prepares briefings, talking points, event flow documents for gatherings and follow-up.

The Principal Responsibilities listed below are generic in nature. Applicants will find the information in this Position Focus to be most relevant to the position.

Required Skills And Abilities

Exceptional communication skills with special emphasis on advanced writing ability and editing. Demonstrated excellent interpersonal skills necessary to communicate effectively by phone and in writing with donors, volunteers and Yale colleagues. Writing sample required at time of interview.
Demonstrated organizational and research abilities with strong attention to detail, including analyzing large volumes of information from disparate sources and synthesizing it in a cogent and concise form.
Advanced proficiency with MS Word and Excel and the ability to conduct data analysis and work with financial information. Knowledge of PowerPoint and Adobe Acrobat. Ability and willingness to develop proficiency with other software including planned giving software.
Demonstrated ability to prioritize work, manage multiple tasks, and meet deadlines in a time-constrained environment. Ability to initiate and complete tasks with minimal supervision. Professionalism, maturity, and the ability to maintain strict confidentiality.
Commitment to an inclusive workplace. Ability to engage with diverse audiences (age, gender, nationality, race/ethnicity, profession, sexual orientation, etc.).

Preferred Skills And Abilities

Experience in a university setting or with development work, familiarity with Yale.
Experience with database software and reporting.

Principal Responsibilities

Drafts a variety of written materials, including detailed individual prospect briefings and endowed gift agreement, proposals in support of specific University initiatives and internal and external correspondence that conforms to the style and voice of the sender. 2. Coordinates research on individual donors and the history and status of gift commitments as needed by gift officers and other University officials. Ensures the accuracy of gift acknowledgments and all information communicated to donors and prospects. 3. Prepares reports on prospect pools summarizing giving, status, affiliation and other data points, as needed. 4. Assists in the coordination of special events, including dedications, donor recognition events and celebration of special initiatives to ensure timely and successful completion of the proceedings. 5. Designs and produces ad hoc reports based on data extracted from primary databases to support fund raising programs. 6. Oversees stewardship functions to ensure that donors receive ongoing communication regarding the benefits of their gifts to Yale. 7. Supports fundraising directors and gift officers in a range of additional activities related to the University’s development effort, as needed. 8. May perform other duties as assigned.

Six years of related work experience, four of them in the same job family at the next lower level and a high school level education; or four years of related work experience and an Associate degree; or little or no work experience and a Bachelor degree in a related field; or an equivalent combination of experience and education.
